interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines state that MRI-directed US-guided prostate biopsy is the standard of care when MRI shows a suspicious lesion. "MRI-directed US-guided prostate biopsy can be performed using either the transperineal or the transrectal approach." This suggests that a biopsy is indicated when the MRI is positive.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED, your bid of BIOPSY p(biopsy) = 0.87 is high, but the guideline treats the PI-RADS score as the primary driver. The guideline suggests that a PI-RADS score of 3 or higher triggers biopsy, which is a variable the guideline makes decisive. The guideline requires the PI-RADS score to be $\ge 3$ to trigger the recommendation. The guideline needs the PI-RADS score to be $\ge 3$ to make a decision, which is a fact the panel already represents.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the prior biopsy status: None means the indication stands, as the guideline does not specify otherwise for this scenario.
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: unchanged does not support re-sampling, new or larger does
psa_trend - the PSA velocity: 0.96 ng/mL/yr indicates a rising trend, which is a factor in clinical suspicion, though not explicitly a threshold in the retrieved text.
laboratory_results - the PSA density: 0.411 ng/mL² is a value that, when combined with the PI-RADS score, informs the clinical context, though the guideline focuses on the PI-RADS score.
